case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
**Pick: Grand Haven.** Expect it to be below average. My ratings are mostly inference, because the reports give little pier detail.

| Port | Pier rating (0–4) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Grand Haven** | **1** (below average) | Medium |
| Muskegon | 1 | Low |
| South Haven | 1 | Low |
| St. Joseph | 0 (slow) | Medium |

**How to fish Grand Haven:** Cast glow spoons at first and last light. The pier reports mention spoons and glow plugs, and low-light casting.

**What the reports say**
- The newest reports are from 2023-08-30, which is 6 days old. Nothing newer exists, so this is a guide and not current conditions.
- **Grand Haven:**
  - Pier anglers caught a few salmon casting spoons in low light (2023-08-30).
  - Pier results were a few salmon on glow spoons (2023-08-23, rated 1), a slow bite on glow spoons and plugs (2023-08-16, rated 0), and a few on glow plugs (2023-08-02, rated 1).
  - Boats did better. They found good action in 40–80 ft of water on glow or chrome J-plugs and white flasher/flies (2023-08-30, rated 3).
- **St. Joseph:** Pier anglers targeting trout and salmon had slow fishing (2023-08-30, rated 0). Earlier, pier fishing was "a little on the slow side," with a few coho on nightcrawlers (2023-08-09, rated 1). Few boats got out the week of 2023-08-30 because of poor weather.
- **Muskegon:** There are no pier or breakwall salmon reports this summer. Boats found the bite slow (2023-08-30, rated 0), and salmon had "slowed down" the week before (2023-08-23).
- **South Haven:** There are no pier reports this summer. Boats were slow (2023-08-30, rated 0), with scattered fish around 100 ft (2023-08-23). That week's text also says fishing was "pretty good when boat anglers made it out," which conflicts with the 0 rating. The Black River salmon trolling was very slow (2023-08-30).
- **Access:** None of the reports mention closed piers or launches.

**Water:** The conditions tool only gave a buoy summary for the week before today, with no wind forecast, pierhead model or cold-layer data.
- Surface water averaged about 63 F at the Grand Haven and Muskegon buoy, 68 F at South Haven and 71 F at St. Joseph.
- The Grand Haven and Muskegon buoy was up 12 F over the week. The 2023-08-30 reports had flagged a possible upwelling there (down 11 F), so that cold water seems to be warming again.

**History (earlier seasons, same time of year)**
- In early September 2022, pier salmon fishing was slow at Grand Haven (2022-09-07, 2022-09-14) and Muskegon (2022-09-07: "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls").
- Boats had fair to good fishing in those same weeks.
- I found no pier salmon reports for South Haven or St. Joseph in those weeks.

**My read**
- I'd expect pier salmon fishing to be slow everywhere this week. Pier reports this summer were rated 0–1, and early September last year was also slow.
- Grand Haven is my pick because it is the only port with pier salmon catches in several recent reports, and its water is the coolest.
- I'd expect St. Joseph to be the weakest. It has the warmest water, a slow pier report and nothing better to point to.
- A north or east wind that drops the pierhead temperature sharply would be the best sign of a pier bite. That is general guidance from Michigan Sea Grant/MSU Extension, not something the reports say. I couldn't get a wind forecast, so check one before you go.
- Salmon are typically staging for their fall runs by mid-September, but I have no report that confirms that for this week.
